entities.name: Gennadius of Massilia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gennadius of Massilia, also known as Gennadius Scholasticus or Gennadius Massiliensis, was a prominent Christian priest, monk, and historian who flourished in the late 5th century CE, dying around 496 CE in Massilia (modern Marseille). His enduring significance stems primarily from his monumental work, *De viris illustribus* ('On Illustrious Men'), a biographical dictionary of Christian authors that served as a crucial continuation of Jerome's earlier work. Gennadius stands as a vital bridge for understanding the intellectual landscape of early Christianity, meticulously cataloging the lives and writings of over ninety ecclesiastical figures from the late 4th and 5th centuries, a period marked by profound theological debates and the decline of the Western Roman Empire.

His *De viris illustribus* meticulously details the lives and works of Christian writers, theologians, and ascetics, beginning where Jerome left off around 392 CE and extending through his own time. This invaluable text provides insights into figures like Augustine of Hippo, John Cassian, and other less-known but regionally significant thinkers, offering not merely biographical sketches but also critical assessments of their literary styles and theological positions. Beyond this magnum opus, Gennadius authored several other theological works, including an eight-book treatise against all heresies and a six-book work against Nestorius, though these have largely been lost to time, underscoring the singular importance of his surviving biographical compilation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gennadius of Massilia's *De viris illustribus* is a cornerstone of early Christian literary history, preserving vital biographical and bibliographical information for over 90 authors from the late 4th and 5th centuries, thereby becoming an indispensable source for subsequent medieval scholarship and modern historical understanding of the era.
